minimum_basis: Judgment call: Thumbtack's low end for a whole install is $133 and Fixr starts a takedown at $125 a project, so a small job (one window, one short run) still covers the ladder, the drive and the takedown visit.
base: Flat prices are for a one-story home up to 2,200 sq ft, about 150 to 225 ft of roofline (Fixr); the home size and stories factors scale them. The per-foot rates price what you measured, run by run, in the Roofline plan.

packages.label: Full-service light install
includes: Commercial LED lights supplied for the season
Any bulb that goes out fixed during the season
Taken down and stored in January
packages.basis: Light rental packages that include the lights, the install and the takedown: Fixr $200 to $600, HomeAdvisor $250 to $600, Bob Vila $200 to $550. Fixr's average for a 1,500 sq ft home is $450, the middle of this range. Minutes: Bob Vila puts an average home at 1 to 4 hours, plus about an hour for the takedown (judgment call).

sources.says: Light rental averages $200 to $600, including installation; LED rental about $550 for 150 linear feet installed. About $450 on average for a 1,500 sq ft home, which needs at least 150 linear feet.
Christmas light rental packages cost $250 to $600, including installation and takedown for a basic setup; the pro supplies the lights, installs them and removes them after the season.
The total cost for light rental, installation and takedown is typically $200 to $550. It takes 1 to 4 hours to install Christmas lights on an average-size home.

packages.label: Install and takedown of your lights
includes: Your lights tested before they go up
Clipped and hung straight, no nails or tape
Taken down and boxed in January
packages.basis: About 150 ft of roofline at $1.50 to $3 a foot, where Fixr's labor range ($1.50 to $3.50 a foot) and Thumbtack's range for lights you already own ($1.25 to $3 a foot) overlap. Most companies include the takedown in the install price (Fixr).

sources.says: Labor runs $1.50 to $3.50 per linear foot, and the strands add $0.50 to $1.50. Most companies include the cost of removal in the installation packages, and removal costs the same whether the lights are yours or the company's.
Average installation fees are $1.25 to $3 per linear foot of lights if you already own the lights; removal typically costs about half of the install, and some installers include it.

packages.label: Light takedown
includes: Gutters checked for clips left behind
packages.basis: Fixr: removal $125 to $350 a project; HomeAdvisor: $100 to $400 when you hung them yourself. The range is where the two overlap.

sources.says: Christmas light removal costs $125 to $350 per project or $0.50 to $0.65 per linear foot.
If you put them up and want someone else to take them down, you pay $100 to $400 or roughly $0.50 per linear foot.

packages.label: By the foot, with my lights
includes: Lights, install, fixes during the season, takedown and storage
packages.basis: Where HomeAdvisor's per-foot range ($2.50 to $7, covering the lights, set-up and removal) and Fixr's ($2 to $5 a foot, materials and labor) overlap. Minutes: Bob Vila's 1 to 4 hours for an average home plus the takedown, about 1.4 minutes a foot (judgment call).

sources.says: Christmas light pros charge $2.50 to $7 per linear foot; that covers the lights, set-up, removal and sometimes mid-season maintenance.
Installation runs $2 to $5 per foot for materials and labor; about 65% of the cost is labor and 35% materials.

packages.label: By the foot, hanging your lights
packages.basis: Where Fixr's labor range ($1.50 to $3.50 a foot) and Thumbtack's range for lights the customer owns ($1.25 to $3 a foot) overlap. Thumbtack: most installers charge twice as much for the second story, so the Roofline plan adds this rate again for upper-story runs.

sources.says: Labor runs $1.50 to $3.50 per linear foot of the total price.

$1.25 to $3 per linear foot of lights if you already own the lights; most installers charge twice as much to hang lights on the second story as on the first, and a hard-to-reach roof may cost an additional 20 percent.

packages.label: By the foot, takedown
includes: Taking down and boxing lights the customer owns
packages.basis: Fixr: $0.50 to $0.65 a linear foot; HomeAdvisor: roughly $0.50 a linear foot.

sources.says: Christmas light removal costs $125 to $350 per project or $0.50 to $0.65 per linear foot.
Taking down lights someone else put up costs $100 to $400 or roughly $0.50 per linear foot.

packages.label: Lights to keep, by the foot
includes: The lights, sold to the customer to keep
packages.basis: Thumbtack, HomeAdvisor and Bob Vila all put lights the installer supplies at about $0.50 to $2 a foot on top of the install (HomeAdvisor from $0.40).

sources.says: If you want the company installing your lights to provide them, expect to pay between 50 cents and $2 per linear foot for the strands of lights alone.
Christmas light prices run $0.40 to $2 per linear foot when purchased as part of the installation; if you don't own lights, add $0.50 to $2 per foot.
To include the holiday lights themselves in the project, expect to pay an additional $0.50 to $2 per linear foot.

factors.label: Home size
factors.basis: Fixr, one story: 1,000 to 2,000 sq ft $225 to $500; 2,400 and 3,200 sq ft $330 to $600 (about 1.2 times the 1,500 sq ft middle); 4,200 sq ft $375 to $625 (about 1.3 times). Bob Vila: 1,000 sq ft $250 to $600, 2,000 sq ft $300 to $750, 4,000 sq ft $500 to $1,800.

sources.says: By home size: 1,000 sq ft $250 to $600; 2,000 sq ft $300 to $750; two-story 1,500 sq ft $400 to $1,000; two-story 2,500 sq ft $500 to $1,200; 4,000 sq ft $500 to $1,800.

factors.label: Stories
factors.basis: Fixr at 1,500 sq ft: one story $275 to $475, two stories $425 to $630, three stories $525 to $750, about 1.4 and 1.7 times. Thumbtack: most installers charge twice as much for the second story, so these are on the low side. HomeAdvisor: multi-story homes can reach $1,300.

sources.says: 1,500 sq ft: one story $275 to $475, two stories $425 to $630, three stories $525 to $750. Homes with many levels and hard-to-reach eaves run about 20% to 25% above regular installation costs.
Most installers charge twice as much to hang lights on the second story of a home as on the first.
Average installation $220 to $684; multi-story homes can reach $1,300. Plan on paying 20% more for hard-to-reach roofs and eaves.

addons.label: Small tree wrap, about 6 ft
addons.basis: Fixr and Bob Vila: $75 to $125 in labor for a small tree about 6 ft high.

sources.says: Wrapping an outdoor tree costs $75 to $125 in labor for a small tree of about six feet, $125 to $250 for a medium tree 12 to 18 feet tall, and $300 to $1,500 for a 28 ft tree.
The labor cost to wrap a tree ranges from $75 to $125 for a small tree about 6 feet high up to $300 to $1,500 for a large tree as high as 28 feet; $125 to $250 for a 12 to 18 foot tree.

addons.label: Medium tree wrap, 12 to 18 ft
addons.basis: Fixr and Bob Vila: $125 to $250 for a tree 12 to 18 ft tall. Taller trees may need a lift: price them on site.

sources.says: For a medium-sized tree that is 12 to 18 feet tall, the price will be around $125 to $250; for the largest trees a lift may be needed.
For an average-size tree of 12 to 18 feet, expect to pay $125 to $250.

addons.label: Outdoor light timer
addons.basis: Where Fixr ($12 to $50), HomeAdvisor ($10 to $50) and Bob Vila ($10 to $30) overlap.

sources.says: Timers can be purchased for $12 to $50 each.
Timers run $10 to $50 each.
A holiday light timer costs about $10 to $30.

plans_basis: Fixr: most companies offer 10% to 20% off packages installed before the busy season; HomeAdvisor: booking between February and September often gets lower rates. The every season plan takes the low end, 10%, for booking the same house again (judgment call).

plans_sources.says: If you have lights installed before the busy season starts (after Thanksgiving), most companies offer a 10% to 20% discount on their packages; contact installers many months before Christmas.
Booking between February and September often scores lower rates because demand is light and pros have open calendars; you might negotiate a package that includes removal or storage.
